chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) handed over to me a Mushaf (copy of the Quran) and said: 'Do not look into it.' So I opened it and read in it 'Lam yakulli allatheena kafaroo' [98:1], and I found therein the names of seventy men from Quraish, by their names and the names of their fathers. He said: 'So he sent a message to me: Send to me with the Mushaf.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (a title for an Imam, typically Al-Hasan al-Askari or Al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the names of seventy men from Quraish found in the Mushaf in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the concept of *al-Qira'ah al-Shay'iyyah* (variant readings) preserved in the Umayyad era, where specific names of Quraysh disbelievers were inserted into the text of Surah Al-Bayyinah (98:1) to personalize the condemnation. The Imam’s instruction not to read it initially suggests a focus on the textual variant itself rather than the recitation, serving as evidence for the validity of multiple canonical readings (*Qira'at*) within the Shia tradition. The return of the Mushaf underscores the careful preservation of these specific textual variations by the Imams.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassanasws handed over a Parchment to me and said: ‘Do not look into it’. But I opened it and read in it [98:1] Those who disbelieved, so I found therein names of seventy men from Qureysh, by their names and the names of their fathers. So heasws sent a message to me: ‘Send someone to (return to) me with the Parchment’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain individuals of his people from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“Once, abu al-Hassan (a.s.) gave me a copy of the Holy Quran saying, ‘Do not look at it.’ I opened and read in it (Chapter 98) ‘The unbelievers were not . . .’ and I found therein the names of seventy people from Quraysh with their names and the names of their fathers.’ The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) sent a message to me, ‘Send the copy back to me.’”
